document_title: VisionNav Robotics full-line catalog, Spanish edition — 'Catalog-Spainish-2024V1.2' (document version string printed on p.1). 16 pages.
researcher_notes:
SCOPE: this file covers the ONE remaining never-extracted VisionNav document, 1728979799.pdf. It had been spot-checked in an earlier session and written off as 'confirmatory only, low value'. THAT ASSESSMENT IS WRONG and should be discarded: the catalog carries a full 30-row technical parameter table for every model, and the DB rows it maps onto currently hold only ~12 populated fields each. It yields 13 product entries (1 genuinely new model, VNR14) and roughly 25 fields per product, most of them previously NULL.

DOCUMENT GENERATION: this is the OLDER VisionNav generation — model codes carry the -01/-07 suffixes and the (V)/(VL)/(VM) navigation-package markers, and the layout is metric-first with a parenthesised imperial column. Per the VisionNav model-code convention, (VL) decodes as 'Vision-based Navigation + 3D Laser Navigation'. Every model in this catalog is (VL), i.e. there is no magnetic-guided (VM) machine here, so infrastructure_free=true is safe throughout.

*** SYSTEMATIC FINDING #1 — the lifting_height 'conflicts' are one single reference-mast artefact, not eight independent errors. ***
Eight products (VNSL14, VNP15, VNP20, VNP30, VNE20, VNE30, VNE35, VNE40) show DB lifting_height that disagrees with this catalog. In every case the DB holds the value from footnote *1 — the REFERENCE MAST the rest of the spec table is measured with — while the catalog's 'Altura de elevación' row states the MAXIMUM available mast. The proof is VNSL14: its footnote reads 'un mástil dúplex de 1600 mm (63 pulg.)' and the DB holds exactly 1600. Every P- and E-series footnote reads 'mástil dúplex de 118 pulgadas (3000 mm)' and the DB holds exactly 3000 for all seven of them. This is a configuration axis, not a data error on either side.
I have NOT proposed overwriting any of them. AP0's lifting_height hint states no direction (unlike max_payload's 'heaviest' or min_aisle_width's 'minimum'), so per the no-blanket-conservatism rule I fall back to conservative — and the conservative value is the one already stored. What the Tech Lead actually needs to decide is whether AP0 should store the reference-mast height or the max-mast height, because footnote *4 on every single page says the maximum mast DERATES the payload ('mayores alturas de elevación pueden dar lugar a una disminución de la capacidad'), so storing max lift together with max payload overstates the machine on two K.O. fields at once. This is the payload-derating problem again, now with an eight-product worked example in one document.

*** SYSTEMATIC FINDING #2 — a mislabelled row in the Spanish edition. ***
On EVERY spec page (8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16) the humidity row is printed with the WRONG LABEL: it reads 'Separación interior entre horquillas' (inner fork spread) but carries the value '20% ~ 95%'. The correct inner-fork-spread row, in millimetres, already appears earlier on the same page. The row sits between 'Temperatura de Trabajo' and 'Planicidad del suelo', which is exactly where the working-humidity row sits in VisionNav's English sheets, and the English sheets independently give 20%~95% there. I have therefore mapped it to operating_humidity_max=95 for all 13 products, but I am flagging it loudly because it is a defect in the source document itself, not an extraction artefact — anyone re-reading this PDF will see the wrong label.

*** SYSTEMATIC FINDING #3 — the p.7 series matrix is the most useful page in the document and it is invisible to text extraction. ***
p.7 is a 6-series x 11-criterion capability matrix (load types x application types). pdfplumber linearises it into a meaningless column of isolated tick marks; it only becomes readable as a 160 dpi render. It is the ONLY place in the entire VisionNav corpus that states, per series, which load carriers and which applications each machine is qualified for. It is the source for load_type, station_applications, trailer_loading/unloading, outdoor_capable and forks_free_floating throughout this file. Two things it settles:
  (a) forks_free_floating — 'Pallet CHEP cerrado' (closed-bottom pallet) is ticked for ST, P, E and R series but explicitly NOT for the SL (slim stacker) series. That is direct manufacturer evidence for the industry README's straddle-under-load rule, and it is also a real data point for the OPEN forks_free_floating contradiction (config/fields.json vs the README disagree on reach trucks): VisionNav says its reach trucks DO handle closed-bottom pallets. I have left forks_free_floating NULL for the R series pending the ruling rather than picking a side.
  (b) stacking_capability — the matrix cleanly separates 'Apilado de mercancías' (goods stacking) from 'Almacén de gran altura' (high-bay warehousing), which is precisely the distinction industry README §6a draws. It ticks stacking ONLY for the P and E series. Read literally that makes stacking_capability=false for the SL and R series, yet the DB holds 1 for VNSL14, VNR16 and VNR20 and the SL machine is literally called an 'apilador' (stacker). I judged that too aggressive to propose as a value, so I have left stacking_capability out of the fields block for those three products and flagged it instead. It needs a Tech Lead call.

*** THE RECURRING no-Forklift-turning-radius GAP, again, with nine more instances. ***
Every forklift page prints 'Radio Mínimo de Giro' — explicitly a RADIUS in Spanish, so unambiguous and safe to map — and there is still no turning-radius field in Forklift scope (turning_radius is Tugger-only, min_turning_radius is AMR-only). Nine values are stranded here: VNSL14 1137, VNST20 1431, VNP15 1490, VNP20 1900, VNP30 2020, VNR14 1695, VNR16 1800, VNR20 1915, VNE20 1835, VNE30/35/40 2240. The one model that DOES have a home for it (VNQ50, a tugger) is mapped. This document is now the best single artefact for that AP0 gap after 1657089341.pdf.

OTHER FIELDS THAT HAD NOWHERE TO GO: 'Planicidad del suelo' is printed for all 13 models and spans ±3, ±5 and ±10 mm/m² within this one catalog — a 3x spread that floor_flatness_req's four categorical values cannot hold, so all 13 are left NULL. Body weight (500–6200 kg) is printed for every model and has no AP0 field. Battery voltage/capacity architecture (24V/48V/83.2V) likewise. 'Materiales sin soporte' (unsupported/pallet-less material) is a load type with no AP0 allowed value.

MAPPING DECISIONS WORTH CHALLENGING: 'Pallet CHEP cerrado' -> Pallet ISO (the catalog's own reference load is 1200x1000 mm, which is ISO; there is no closed-bottom-pallet concept in AP0's load_type list). 'Jaula de almacenaje/estantería multicapa' (mesh storage cage / multi-layer stillage) -> Bulk Bin as the nearest allowed value. Both are noted per product.

company_wide_context.notes:
NOT MAPPED, deliberately:
- outdoor_capable: p.6 claims the positioning module has 'Alta adaptabilidad al entorno: Operaciones en interiores y exteriores'. That is a claim about the NAVIGATION MODULE, not about any vehicle's environmental rating, and the p.7 matrix ticks 'Transporte interior y exterior' for the Q series ONLY. I have set outdoor_capable=true on VNQ50 alone and left it NULL everywhere else rather than fanning the p.6 sentence out.
- languages_spoken: the mere existence of a Spanish-language catalog is real but indirect evidence of ES sales support. The DB currently holds the non-conforming string 'unknown' in this field (allowed values are DE|EN|FR|ES|ZH), which is worth cleaning up regardless. Not proposed as a value.
- service_coverage: p.4 states 'Ventas, Operaciones y Servicios en más de 30 países y regiones' with branches in Rotterdam (Europe), Atlanta, Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore and Hong Kong. This supports a broad footprint but names no individual countries, so no ISO codes can be derived. IMPORTANT related finding: p.16 restricts the VNQ50 to the Americas only, which contradicts that product's stored service_coverage of 'EU' — see the VNQ50 entry.
- vda5050_compatible: 'VDA 5050' does not appear anywhere in this document. Left NULL per the field's NULL RULE.
- fleet_management_system: RCS 2.0 is a named proprietary controller that also exposes a REST API. The single-select cannot express 'proprietary product with an open API', which is a known AP0 limitation. Not mapped.
- reference_count: p.2 claims 'cientos de instalaciones' (hundreds of installations) and 'más de 11 millones de almacenamientos de pallets' and 'decenas de empresas de la lista Fortune 500'. These are marketing magnitudes, not a countable reference figure. Not mapped.
- The perception module's stated capability (p.6: '±10 mm y ±0.5°' 6-DoF pose detection) matches the per-model 'Precisión de Ubicación' rows exactly, which is a useful cross-check that the per-product stop_accuracy values are consistent with the platform-level claim.

R-series shared (p.13, single 3-model configuration table verified against a 150 dpi pdftoppm render because several cells are MERGED across models and pdfplumber's linearisation cannot show the merge boundaries): reference mast per footnote *1 = 'mástil triple telescópico de 5755 mm (225 pulg.)' → mast_type Triplex (note: 225 in = 5715 mm, so the printed 5755 mm is itself ~40 mm off — a source rounding/typo, cited as printed). Footnote *2 states optional masts / attachments / larger loads / greater lift heights reduce capacity. navigation_type = Vision, NOT SLAM: the 'Método de Posicionamiento' row reads 'Vision-based' for the whole R series, whereas every other series in this catalog reads '3D SLAM'. ('Lidar 3D' on the next row is the PERCEPTION method for load handling, not positioning.) The (VL) code suffix decodes as 'Vision + 3D Laser' per the VisionNav model-code convention, so a case could be made for ['Vision','Natural Feature (SLAM)'] — but only 'Vision-based' is printed, and one vendor compound term maps to one AP0 value. products.notes: DB CONFLICT ×3 (do not overwrite, all flagged for manual resolution): (1) DB towing_capacity=19958 vs catalog 5000. UNIT FORENSICS: 19958 kg is EXACTLY 44,000 lb (44000 × 0.45359237 = 19958.06), so the DB value came from a US-market imperial spec sheet, not from a metric source — it is not a random error. This catalog prints 5000kg (11000lb), i.e. exactly one QUARTER of 44,000 lb. A plausible reconciliation is that 5000 kg is the tractor's rated drawbar/tow rating and 44,000 lb is a total train weight, but the catalog does not say so. Needs a Tech Lead call. (2) DB max_payload=5000. Per the established VisionNav tow-tractor rule, a tow tractor's 'Rated Load Capacity' is a TRACTION rating and max_payload should be NULL — this page corroborates that rule: it has no fork, mast or lift row at all, and instead gives 'Altura central del bulón de tracción' (traction-pin centre height) and 'Tracción nominal en la barra de tracción 1000N' (rated drawbar pull). I have deliberately NOT proposed a max_payload value. (3) DB service_coverage='EU', but p.16 states in a boxed note: 'Este producto solo está disponible en América. Contacta a tu representante de ventas... para conocer la disponibilidad más reciente.' (This product is only available in the Americas.) That directly contradicts an EU service-coverage claim for this specific model. This is the single most commercially significant finding in the file. DB max_speed=2.0 CONFIRMED (metric). SOURCE INCONSISTENCY: the imperial column prints '2.90mph' for 2.0 m/s, but 2.0 m/s = 4.47 mph; 2.90 mph would be 1.30 m/s. Every other page in this catalog converts 2.0 m/s correctly to 4.47 mph, so this is a p.16-local typo in the imperial column; the metric figure is reliable. DB min_aisle_width=1700 appears to have been populated from 'Min. Pasillo de giro (sin carrito) 1700mm' — that is a min TURNING-aisle figure measured WITHOUT a cart, not a working aisle width, and the established VisionNav convention is not to map turning-aisle rows to min_aisle_width. Flagged, not changed. coupling_type left NULL: the page names a traction pin ('bulón de tracción') but never states whether coupling is automatic or manual, so 'Pintle Hook' would be a guess. max_trailers left NULL: not stated anywhere. UNMAPPED (no AP0 field): body weight 1000kg; battery 24V/270Ah LiFePO4; wheelbase 1050mm; rated drawbar pull 1000N; motor power 3kW (60-min rating); electromagnetic service brake; noise at operator's ear <70dB; traction-pin centre height options 290/345/400mm; max joint width 30mm; max obstacle height 20mm; floor flatness ±5mm/㎡.
